questions.stem: A can do a piece of work in 10 days, B in 15 days. How many days will they take working together?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A's rate = 1/10 work/day. B's rate = 1/15 work/day. Combined = 1/10+1/15 = 3/30+2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6. Time = 6 days. **Short Trick:** Together = (A×B)/(A+B) = (10×15)/(10+15) = 150/25 = 6 days.

questions.stem: A can do a job in 12 days. After working 4 days, B joins. They finish the remaining work in 4 days. In how many days can B alone do the job?
questions.explanation: A is correct. A alone for 4 days: completes 4/12 = 1/3 of work. Remaining = 2/3. A+B finish 2/3 in 4 days → their combined rate = (2/3)/4 = 1/6 per day. 1/B = 1/6 − 1/12 = 2/12 − 1/12 = 1/12. B alone takes 12 days.

questions.stem: 20 workers can build a wall in 30 days. How many workers are needed to build it in 12 days?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Men × Days = Work (constant). 20 × 30 = W × 12. W = 600/12 = 50 workers. Inverse proportion: more workers → fewer days. **Short Trick:** New workers = original workers × (original days / new days) = 20 × (30/12) = 20 × 2.5 = 50.

questions.stem: A does twice as much work as B in the same time. If together they can finish a job in 18 days, how long does A alone take?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Let B do x work/day. A does 2x work/day. Together: 3x = 1/18 → x = 1/54. A's rate = 2/54 = 1/27. A alone takes 27 days. Verify: 1/27+1/54 = 2/54+1/54 = 3/54 = 1/18 ✓.

questions.stem: A, B, and C can complete a work in 20, 30, and 60 days respectively. A works every day, B works every alternate day (days 2,4,6...), and C works every third day (days 3,6,9...). How many days to complete the work?
If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days, and 26 men and 48 boys can do the same in 2 days, how long will 15 men and 20 boys take?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Let m = man's daily rate, b = boy's. From equations: 6m+8b = 1/10; 26m+48b = 1/2. Multiply first by 6: 36m+48b = 6/10. Subtract second: 10m = 6/10−1/2 = 1/10 → m = 1/100. From first: 6/100+8b=1/10 → 8b = 1/10−6/100 = 4/100 → b = 1/200. Rate of 15m+20b = 15/100+20/200 = 15/100+10/100 = 25/100 = 1/4. Time = 4 days.

questions.stem: A contractor undertook to complete a road in 60 days, employing 30 workers. After 20 days, 2/3 of the work was still remaining. How many additional workers must he hire to complete the work on time?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 30 workers complete 1/3 of the work in 20 days. Total man-days for full job = 30×20×3 = 1800. Remaining work = 2/3 requires 1200 man-days. Available time = 60−20 = 40 days. Workers needed = 1200/40 = 30. He already has 30 workers — no additional needed. The trap is assuming more workers are needed when the original workforce is actually sufficient.

questions.stem: A and B can complete a job in 12 days. B and C in 15 days. A and C in 20 days. How many days will A, B, and C working together take?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Adding all three pairs: (A+B)+(B+C)+(A+C) = 2(A+B+C). 1/12+1/15+1/20 = 5/60+4/60+3/60 = 12/60 = 1/5. So 2(A+B+C) = 1/5 → A+B+C = 1/10. Together they take 10 days. **Short Trick:** Sum of three pairwise rates = twice the combined rate. Find half of that sum.

questions.stem: A alone can do a job in 16 days. A works for 4 days, then leaves. B completes the remaining work in 18 days. How many days would B take alone to complete the full job?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A's rate = 1/16/day. In 4 days: A completes 4/16 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4 of the job. B completes 3/4 in 18 days → B's rate = (3/4)/18 = 1/24/day. B alone takes 24 days. **Short Trick:** B's time = 18 ÷ (3/4) = 18 × 4/3 = 24.

questions.stem: Efficiency of A is 50% more than B. If together they complete work in 12 days, how many days does A take alone?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A is 50% more efficient than B → A's rate = 1.5 × B's rate. Let B's rate = x. A's rate = 1.5x. Together: 2.5x = 1/12 → x = 1/30 (B takes 30 days). A's rate = 1.5/30 = 1/20. A alone takes 20 days. **Short Trick:** Ratio A:B = 3:2 (efficiency). Together in 12 days → B alone = 12×(3+2)/2 = 30; A alone = 12×(3+2)/3 = 20.
